notes: Subject-object insert. Annihilation is a firm rule over antiparticle_of (relation can_annihilate_with); the charge, mass and spin queries carry values across the relation (fol). Relations once declared in this file are catalogued in RELATIONS.md since 2026-10-30.

queries.not_checked: fol (arithmetic): opposite charge of a given value
fol: equal mass carried across the relation (a value comparison)
fol: equal spin carried across the relation (a value comparison)

fol.notes: The three laws of antiparticles are firm rules over antiparticle_of; the prompt's value about the pelquon is a given fact. q3 (annihilation) is dl (HermiT).

opposite_charge.says: A particle and its antiparticle have opposite electric charges.

same_mass.says: A particle and its antiparticle have the same mass.
same_mass.z3: ForAll([a, b], Implies(antiparticle_of(a, b), mass_gev(a) == mass_gev(b)))

same_spin.says: A particle and its antiparticle have the same spin.
same_spin.z3: ForAll([a, b], Implies(antiparticle_of(a, b), spin(a) == spin(b)))

pelquon_charge.says: The pelquon has an electric charge of −1 e.

pelquon_mass.says: The pelquon has a mass of 3.2 GeV/c².

label_corrections.why: No arithmetic: the mass is carried unchanged across antiparticle_of. With the mass as a named value (3.2 GeV/c²) and a functional has-mass relation, the firm SWRL rule antiparticle_of(?a, ?b), has_mass(?b, ?m) -> has_mass(?a, ?m) gives it, as the DL file's annihilation rule does.
As q1: the spin is carried unchanged across antiparticle_of; a named value and a SWRL rule suffice.
